This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and reserv  orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal K  Paliwal pronounced the following:

ORDER This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 10.05.2022 passed by MACT, Mandsaur in Claim Case No.297/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

2. As per the findings of the Tribunal, for the death of Mahendra Chandel, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,29,000/- along with interest, however, deducted 40% amount under the head of contributory negligence and paid a sum of Rs.6,77,400/-.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 Loss of dependency -Rs.7,20,000/
 Future prospects -Rs.2,88,000/
 Loss of consortium -Rs.88,000/-
Nojibai vs Dilip on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179955219/
2  Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.11,29,000/-
Less 40% towards  contributory negligence -Rs.4,51,600/-
Learned counsel for appellants submits that tribunal has wrongly determined deceased's income at Rs.5000/- per month.
It should have assessed deceased's income at Rs.6500/- per month.
Further, tribunal has also erred in holding that it is a case of contributory negligence.
Learned counsel, after referring to Para-15 of impugned award and spot map exhibit P8 submits that at the time of accident, deceased was going on on his left side/correct side of road.
It is also evident from above that accident did not occur in the middle of the road, instead, it occurred on the side of the road.
No cross-case has been registered against the deceased.
It is also urged that it is not correct that in appeal memo, there are no averments that tribunal's findings with respect to contributory negligence on the part of deceased is wrong.
Hence, it cannot be said that it is a case of contributory negligence on the part of deceased.

In view of above, learned tribunal has wrongly assessed 40%
contributory negligence on the part of deceased.

On above grounds, it is submitted that appeal be allowed and compensation be assessed by taking deceased's monthly income at Rs 6,500/- per month and by not deducting any amount for contributory negligence.
4. Learned counsel for respondents submits that learned tribunal has rightly determined deceased's income at Rs. 5,000/- per month.
PW/1 and PW/2 have admitted in their depositions that both the vehicles have collided head-on.
Hence, in para 17 of impugned award, learned tribunal has drawn correct findings.
In appeal memo, there are no averments that findings recorded by tribunal regarding contributory negligence are not correct.
Thus, there is no illegality in the findings recorded by tribunal.
Hence, appeal be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

6. Perusal of submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and grounds taken in the appeal memo shows that appellant has challenged impugned award primarily on two grounds, i.e.
deceased's income has not been correctly assessed and that tribunal has wrongly concluded that deceased also contributed to the happening of accident.
Nojibai vs Dilip on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179955219/
3 7.
So far as occupation and income of deceased is concerned, as per Nauji Bai (Aw-1), deceased was working as labourer and thereby earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
Present accident pertains to the year 2018.
Therefore, it would be just and proper to consider/accept deceased's per month income as Rs.6500/-.
8. Next question before this court is whether deceased in any way contributed to the happening of present accident.
Claimant witnesses Rampyari and Toofan Singh have deposed in their examination in chief that motor cycle coming from front, hit deceased's motor cycle by going in the wrong direction.

Perusal of cross examination of above claimant witnesses reveal that their above testimony has not been challenged in the cross-examination and no specific suggestion has been given to them that when accident, occurred, deceased was riding his motorcycle on the wrong side of the road and non-applicant Dileep was riding his motorcycle on his left side/correct side of the road.

Learned Tribunal in para-15 of impugned award, after referring to spot map exhibit P6, has opined that as per spot map exhibit P6 deceased was going on on his left side and he was hit by the motorcycle coming from the front.
Further, perusal of spot map exhibit P6 reveals that accident did not occur in the middle of the road, instead, it has occurred on the side of the road.

9. It is correct that applicant witness Rampyari has stated in her cross- examination that Mahendra was hit by the motor cycle coming from the front and that both the motorcycles have collided head-on.
With respect to Rampyari's above statement in her cross-examination, it has to be kept in mind that a witness' testimony has to be read and assessed/appreciated as a whole and not in isolation.
Further, she has denied the suggestion given to him in her cross-examination that Mahendra's motor cycle and other motor cycle had collided in the middle of the road.

Hence, if Rampyari's both examination in chief and cross-examination, as discussed above, are read/appreciated as a whole, then, just on the basis of Rampyari's above statement in her cross-examination, it cannot be held that it is a case of head on collision.

10. Therefore, in view of discussion and analysis of evidence on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, conclusions drawn by tribunal in para-15 to 18 of impugned award are contrary to evidence on record.
Hence, they cannot be sustained.
Thus, in the instant case, from evidence on record, it is not established that deceased in any way contributed to the happening of present accident.
Therefore, no deductions can be made on account of contributory negligence on the part of deceased.
11. There is no dispute with respect to age of deceased, multiplier and deductions for personal expenses.

Therefore, on taking deceased's monthly income as Rs.6,500/- loss of dependency would be as under :-
Loss of dependency -Rs.9,36,000/- (i.e. Rs.6500x12=78000 - 1/3 personal expenses=52000 x 18 (multiplier))
12.
There is also no dispute with respect to compensation under various other conventional heads as awarded by tribunal.

Hence, total compensation, including compensation under various conventional heads, would be as under :-
Nojibai vs Dilip on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179955219/
4  Loss of dependency -Rs.9,36,000/-
 Future prospects (40%) -Rs.3,74,400/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.88,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
13. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.14,31,400/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,77,400/- (after deducting 40% towards contributory negligence).
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.7,54,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
14. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.7,54,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

15. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.2 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount of Rs.5,54,000/- the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimants shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
16. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE hk/
